### Given Data
- Width of the box ($L$) = $2.5 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$
- Mass of an electron ($m$) = $9.11 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$
- Lowest permitted energy level ($n$) = $1$
- Planck's constant ($h$) = $6.626 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J}\,\text{s}$

### Formula
The energy eigenenergies for a 1-D infinite potential box are given by:
$$E_n = \frac{n^2 h^2}{8 m L^2}$$

### Calculation
For the lowest energy state ($n = 1$):
$$E_1 = \frac{1^2 \times (6.626 \times 10^{-34})^2}{8 \times (9.11 \times 10^{-31}) \times (2.5 \times 10^{-10})^2}$$

$$E_1 = \frac{4.39\times 10^{-67}}{8 \times 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \times 6.25 \times 10^{-20}}$$

$$E_1 = \frac{4.39 \times 10^{-67}}{4.555 \times 10^{-49}} \approx 9.64 \times 10^{-19} \text{ J}$$

Converting Joules to electron-volts ($	ext{eV}$):
$$E_1 = \frac{9.64 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 	imes 10^{-19}} \approx 6.02 \text{ eV}$$
